newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, ACCESS skids after AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, ACCESS skids after AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by revised forecasts for more cold next week, ended higher Wednesday in moderate trade, then tumbled on ACCESS after AGA reported an unexpectedly-small weekly stock draw.
February climbed 17.9 cents to close at $3.513 per million British thermal units, then tumbled to $3.40 on ACCESS. March settled 15 cents higher at $3.176. Others also ended higher.

"The change in the forecast helped (firm prices), but what a difference spring makes. We had a week of spring weather last week and no one burned any gas," said one Midwest trader, adding there was some disbelief about the low AGA number.

He was referring to weekly AGA storage data released late Wednesday that showed U.S. gas stocks fell last week by an unexpectedly-small 15 bcf. Earlier, a Reuter poll showed most expected a 70-85 bcf weekly stock draw. Stocks are now 69 bcf above year-ago levels, the first time in more than a year that overall U.S. gas inventories have been in surplus to year-ago.
Eastern storage stands at 211 bcf, or almost 20 percent, over last year.

But traders said revised forecasts calling for a second Canadian cold surge next week behind the current Arctic front should lend some support to futures near-term, particularly with cash still 30 cents over the screen. Originally, forecasters were looking for a warming trend early next week.
Technically, traders still pegged February resistance in the $3.80-3.84 area, then at $3.96 and the contract high of $4.02. Support remained in the $3.11-3.28 gap and then in the $2.60s.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped about five cents Wednesday to the mid-$3.70s. Midcontinent pipes were little changed in the high-$3.80s. New York city gate gas was talked between $4.20 and $4.60, steady to down slightly from Tuesday.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 4.5 cents to $2.504. NYMEX said 41,493 Hub contracts traded, down from Tuesday's revised tally of 49,707.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Wednesday.

On the KCBT, February closed up 11.9 cents at $3.33, while deferred months finished mixed. The East/West spread widened by six cents to 18.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 337 contracts traded, down from Tuesday's total of 413.
